title: Bind model-routing provenance to the authoritative merge SHA

sha_binding.verified_source_note: Final substantive implementation commit. Chain of fixes across seven independent-review rounds, all in scripts/ops/proof-generate.ts, scripts/ops/lane-close.ts, and .github/workflows/post-merge-lane-close.yml: (1) the trusted --repair-merged path now binds every declared model-routing.json sidecar (previously only evidence.json/verification.md), propagating malformed/missing/identity-mismatch/conflicting-binding failures as model_routing_rebind_failed; (2) that path reuses safeRepoPath's repo-root escape guard; (3) post-merge-lane-close.yml's early proof-bind step is restricted to push events, since workflow_dispatch's github.sha is not the historical lane's authoritative SHA; (4) rebindModelRoutingJsonSha requires non-empty model/reasoning_effort fields on any required sidecar, rejecting a truncated or identity-only sidecar; (5) the same workflow step also skips when the checked-out manifest's own commit_sha already disagrees with this push's SHA, closing a second deadlock variant (a governed manifest-only repair PR merging via ordinary push); (6) generateProofArtifacts binds every declared sidecar via .filter(), matching the repair path, instead of only the first via .find(); (7) PM-directed release-blocking correction: rebindModelRoutingJsonSha now validates a required sidecar's model/reasoning_effort exactly against the lane manifest's own model_routing block, and validates model_profile/policy_version whenever both sides carry a value, failing closed with a new sidecar_manifest_routing_mismatch code identifying the offending field before any proof write; (8) a follow-up independent review found the historical fixture tests' manifest-side comparison was tautological (derived from the sidecar it had just read rather than the real lane manifest file) -- both fixture tests now read the real docs/06_status/lanes/<issue>.json manifest directly; (9) an ordinary first-time closeout resolved manifest.pr_url from disk with no GitHub-backed validation before binding model-routing.json's immutable closeout_binding, unlike the trusted repair step that always runs afterward -- a stale/incorrect pr_url (e.g. after a PR rename/reopen) would get baked in permanently before the repair transaction's rollback snapshot is even taken; fixed via a --skip-model-routing option so the workflow's early bind step never touches model-routing.json at all (superseded by (11) below, which closes this for every caller, not just the workflow); (10) rebindModelRoutingJsonSha spread an existing sidecar's fields (including a legacy top-level merge_sha field present in real historical sidecars) unchecked, so a conflicting legacy value could coexist with a newly-appended closeout_binding.merge_sha while P3/C4 both still passed; fixed by failing closed with a new legacy_binding_conflict code when a legacy top-level merge_sha disagrees with the authoritative SHA; (11) the same unvalidated-pr_url risk from (9) still existed for ANY other caller of ops:proof-generate (e.g. an operator manually following proof-repair.ts's printed remediation command), since only the workflow had been given --skip-model-routing; fixed by flipping generateProofArtifacts/ops:proof-generate's default so model-routing.json is never bound unless the caller explicitly opts in with --bind-model-routing (bindModelRouting), which no legitimate caller currently does; (12) the sidecar/manifest routing cross-check from (7) did not validate manual-override provenance, so a sidecar could claim override_used: false (or a different authorizer) while the manifest recorded a manual override and still bind; fixed by requiring the sidecar's override_used/override_authorized_by to agree with the manifest's model_routing.selected_by/override.authorized_by. Post-merge proof generation rebinds this field to the authoritative GitHub merge SHA.

verifier.independence_note: Executor-produced mechanical evidence; this is not PM approval or independent certification.

scope.workflow_change_note: PM-authorized second scope amendment: one-line `if:` condition added to post-merge-lane-close.yml's 'Bind proof artifacts to merge SHA' step (restricts it to push events). No new triggers, permissions, secrets, or jobs added; existing trusted-context validation (isTrustedPostMergeAutomation) and Merge Gate/branch protection are unchanged.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: Post-merge proof generation appends an authoritative closeout binding without replacing execution provenance.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: rebindModelRoutingJsonSha preserves every parsed top-level field, including unknown fields, and adds only closeout_binding with sha_type, merge_sha, pr_url, and bound_at.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: Rebinding is idempotent for the same PR/SHA and fails closed for a different PR or SHA.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: Focused tests prove exact reruns preserve the original bound_at and conflicting PR or merge SHA values throw binding_conflict before any proof write.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: Focused tests cover required missing, invalid JSON, malformed object, missing PR URL, and optional missing cases with distinct fail-closed outcomes.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: Existing evidence and verification rebinding behavior remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: The specialized model-routing preflight is composed with the existing evidence.json and verification Markdown rebinders; the aggregate proof suite passes.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: truth-check-lib focused tests exercise the same sidecar before and after closeout_binding and retain the existing P3/C4 interpretation.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: PM scope amendment: the trusted scripts/ops/lane-close.ts --repair-merged path binds every required model-routing.json sidecar before truth-check, not just evidence.json/verification.md.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: rebindRepairedLaneProof() now validates (write:false) every model-routing.json path declared in expected_proof_paths before writing any proof artifact, then binds it alongside the existing evidence/verification rebind. scripts/ops/lane-close.test.ts proves this against the real UTV2-1585/#1305 and UTV2-1586/#1306 identities, idempotent replay, binding_conflict on a different PR or SHA, malformed_required_sidecar on invalid JSON, sidecar_identity_mismatch on wrong/missing issue_id, missing_required_sidecar when the declared file is absent, no effect on a lane with no declared sidecar, C4/P3 passing through the real path, and rollback of the manifest and every proof file (via the existing createRepairRollbackTransaction, which already snapshots the whole proof directory) when the rebind fails.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: A model-routing rebind failure during trusted repair fails closed with a distinct, propagated error rather than a generic infra_error or silent partial bind.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: main()'s catch block now special-cases ModelRoutingRebindError (checked before the generic fallback) and emits a model_routing_rebind_failed closeout code carrying the underlying model_routing_error_code, proof_path, and message, with transaction.rollback() already invoked unconditionally at the top of that catch block.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: The trusted workflow_dispatch replay path for UTV2-1585/UTV2-1586 does not deadlock model-routing.json's immutable closeout_binding against a non-authoritative SHA before --repair-merged can bind the real one.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: post-merge-lane-close.yml's 'Bind proof artifacts to merge SHA' step is now restricted to push events (github.event_name == 'push'); a workflow-assertion test in scripts/ops/lane-close.test.ts confirms this condition is present.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: A required model-routing sidecar cannot receive an authoritative closeout_binding unless it carries real execution-provenance fields, not merely a matching issue_id.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: rebindModelRoutingJsonSha now requires non-empty model and reasoning_effort string fields on any required sidecar (checked after identity validation, before the existing conflict check). Three new focused tests cover a truncated {issue_id}-only sidecar, a sidecar with reasoning_effort present but blank, and confirm optional (non-required) sidecars remain unaffected.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: A governed manifest-only repair PR merging via an ordinary push (not just a workflow_dispatch replay) does not re-trigger the model-routing deadlock.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: The 'Bind proof artifacts to merge SHA' step now additionally reads the checked-out manifest's own commit_sha and skips the early proof-generate bind whenever it already disagrees with this push's SHA -- the signal that this push is a repair commit (e.g. from buildRepairRequiredViaPrPacket's recommended path), not the lane's own first-time implementation merge. A workflow-assertion test confirms the guard is present and that the pnpm ops:proof-generate call is gated behind it, not run unconditionally alongside it.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: generateProofArtifacts binds every declared model-routing.json sidecar, matching the repair path's already-correct behavior, so a manifest declaring more than one such sidecar cannot get permanently stuck with an unbound second file after a reported-successful proof-generate run.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: Both the validate-pass and write-pass loops in generateProofArtifacts (proof-generate.ts) now iterate every model-routing.json match via .filter() instead of binding only the first via .find(). A regression test proves two sidecars in different subdirectories both receive the closeout_binding.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: A required model-routing sidecar cannot receive an authoritative closeout_binding unless its execution-provenance fields agree with the lane manifest's own model_routing block (PM directive: release-blocking, not a deferred follow-up).
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: rebindModelRoutingJsonSha now requires exact agreement between the sidecar and manifest.model_routing for model and reasoning_effort whenever a manifest model_routing block is supplied, and additionally validates model_profile/policy_version whenever both sides carry a value for them. A mismatch or a manifest-side blank field fails closed with a new sidecar_manifest_routing_mismatch code identifying the offending field, before any proof write. Wired into both generateProofArtifacts and rebindRepairedLaneProof. Nine new focused tests cover: exact match binds; model/reasoning_effort/profile/policy_version mismatches each fail closed; profile/policy_version absent from only one side does not fail; a manifest-side blank field fails closed; a lane with no manifest model_routing block at all is unaffected (ordinary closeout unchanged); a mismatch through the actual trusted repair path rolls back the manifest, evidence, verification, sidecar, and sync/lease/merge-lock state; and the real PR #1305/PR #1306 historical fixtures (read from their actual committed sidecar files) still bind successfully against their real, agreeing manifest routing records.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: model-routing.json's immutable closeout_binding is never written from an unvalidated manifest.pr_url; only the trusted, GitHub-validated repair path binds it, for ANY caller of ops:proof-generate, not just the workflow.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: generateProofArtifacts/ops:proof-generate now default to never binding model-routing.json at all -- binding requires an explicit bindModelRouting option / --bind-model-routing CLI flag, which no current caller sets. (An interim --skip-model-routing flag closed this only for the workflow's own early-bind step; superseded by this default-flip, which closes it for every caller, including a manual operator invocation of the CLI following proof-repair.ts's remediation instructions.) model-routing.json is bound exclusively by ops:lane-close --repair-merged's rebindRepairedLaneProof(), which calls rebindModelRoutingJsonSha directly (not through generateProofArtifacts) using its own GitHub-validated PR/SHA resolution. Focused tests prove the default (no option) never binds or validates model-routing.json, an explicit opt-in still binds correctly, and a workflow-assertion test confirms the early bind step's invocation never passes --bind-model-routing.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: A legacy top-level merge_sha field in a historical sidecar cannot coexist with a conflicting closeout_binding.merge_sha.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: rebindModelRoutingJsonSha now fails closed with a new legacy_binding_conflict code when a sidecar's legacy top-level merge_sha field disagrees with the authoritative merge SHA being bound, before any proof write. A sidecar whose legacy field already agrees is preserved untouched and the closeout_binding is appended normally. Focused tests cover both the conflict (zero mutation) and the agreement case, verified against the real legacy shape present in 14 historical sidecars in the repo.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: A required model-routing sidecar cannot receive an authoritative closeout_binding if its manual-override provenance (override_used, override_authorized_by) misrepresents the lane manifest's own model_routing.selected_by/override.authorized_by.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: rebindModelRoutingJsonSha now requires the sidecar's override_used to agree with whether manifest.model_routing.selected_by is 'manual-override', and when it is, requires override_authorized_by to match manifest.model_routing.override.authorized_by exactly, before any proof write. Five new focused tests cover: override_used disagreement, authorizer disagreement, a manifest recording manual-override with no override.authorized_by, a sidecar missing override_used entirely, and correct agreement binding successfully.

known_limitations: Historical replay of UTV2-1585 and UTV2-1586 is a post-merge follow-up and is not performed by this implementation PR.
The T1 approval label and PM verdict remain independent external merge requirements.

RESOLVED (was a KNOWN GAP): scripts/ops/lane-close.ts's rebindRepairedLaneProof() previously called only rebindMergeSha(), never invoking this issue's model-routing rebind, so a trusted --repair-merged replay of UTV2-1585/UTV2-1586 would still have failed P3/C4 on model-routing.json even after this PR merged. Found by independent Codex review; fixed under a PM-authorized same-lane scope expansion adding scripts/ops/lane-close.ts and scripts/ops/lane-close.test.ts to this issue's file scope. rebindRepairedLaneProof() now validates and binds every declared model-routing.json sidecar before writing any proof artifact, propagating malformed/missing/identity-mismatch/conflicting-binding failures as a new model_routing_rebind_failed closeout code before truth-check runs.

RESOLVED: a fresh independent review of the trusted-repair fix found rebindRepairedLaneProof() resolved manifest-declared model-routing.json paths via a bare path.resolve() with no repo-root escape check, unlike generateProofArtifacts()'s safeRepoPath() guard for the same kind of manifest-declared path. Fixed by exporting and reusing safeRepoPath in lane-close.ts, with a regression test proving an escaping path (e.g. ../../../../tmp/...) is refused.

RESOLVED (was ACCEPTED, not fixed): an independent review first noted that generateProofArtifacts() (proof-generate.ts) bound only the first model-routing.json match via .find() when a manifest declares more than one such sidecar, while rebindRepairedLaneProof() (this PR's earlier fix) bound every match via .filter() -- an inconsistency between the two code paths. Initially left as accepted/deferred since no lane in practice declares more than one such sidecar. A later automated Codex review flagged the same gap as a real correctness defect (the truth gate evaluates every expected proof artifact, so a second sidecar would stay unbound and permanently block closeout even though proof generation reported success), so it was fixed: both the validate-pass and write-pass loops in generateProofArtifacts() now iterate every model-routing.json match via .filter(), matching the repair path. A regression test proves two sidecars under different subdirectories both get bound.

ACCEPTED, not fixed: createRepairRollbackTransaction() snapshots the whole docs/06_status/proof/<issueId>/ directory and relies on every bound model-routing.json sidecar living inside it -- true under the sanctioned lane lifecycle (lane-start.ts always writes proof paths under that directory) but not independently enforced by rebindRepairedLaneProof() or the rollback transaction itself. Combined with the now-fixed path-escape guard, an out-of-directory-but-still-in-repo sidecar path remains a theoretical gap gated behind an already-abnormal, non-lane-start-produced manifest; not fixed here to avoid expanding scope beyond the repair path itself.

RESOLVED (was a second, more severe finding from the same independent review): post-merge-lane-close.yml's 'Bind proof artifacts to merge SHA' step ran unconditionally on both push and workflow_dispatch, passing github.sha as --merge-sha. On workflow_dispatch (the only way to run the trusted --repair-merged replay for UTV2-1585/UTV2-1586) github.sha is main's current tip, not the historical lane's authoritative merge SHA. Because model-routing.json's closeout_binding is intentionally immutable-once-bound (unlike evidence.json/verification.md's last-write-wins rebind), this step would have bound model-routing.json to the wrong SHA on any workflow_dispatch replay attempt, and the immediately-following --repair-merged step's attempt to bind the real SHA would then fail closed with binding_conflict -- permanently deadlocking the exact replay UTV2-1585/UTV2-1586 are queued for. PM authorized a second narrow scope amendment: the step now runs on push events only (github.event_name == 'push'); --repair-merged's own rebindRepairedLaneProof (this issue's fix) already binds model-routing.json authoritatively on the trusted repair path, so the early bind is unneeded there. A regression test asserts the step's if: condition requires github.event_name == 'push'.

ACCEPTED, not fixed: a second fresh-context independent review of the workflow fix noted that the now-skipped-on-workflow_dispatch early bind step used to run the full ops:proof-generate CLI (generateProofArtifacts), which creates diff-summary.md/verification.md from scratch when missing -- unlike rebindRepairedLaneProof()'s rebindMergeSha(), which only rebinds evidence.json/verification.md if they already exist and otherwise reports 'missing' without creating them. A lane that reached a workflow_dispatch --repair-merged replay having never had proof-generate run against it at all (not merely missing SHA binding) would now stay without those files. Not a live issue: both actual replay candidates, UTV2-1585 and UTV2-1586, already have populated evidence.json (with an existing sha_binding object) and verification.md in the repository today, so rebindMergeSha correctly updates them. Left undocumented-until-now theoretical gap for a future lane that skipped normal proof generation entirely before merge -- an already-abnormal state, not fixed here to avoid expanding scope beyond the repair path and the one workflow condition.

RESOLVED: an automated Codex review found rebindModelRoutingJsonSha accepted any required sidecar with a matching issue_id regardless of whether it carried real execution-provenance fields -- a truncated/tampered sidecar such as {"issue_id":"UTV2-1586"} would receive an authoritative closeout_binding despite providing no evidence of which model executed the lane. Fixed by requiring non-empty model and reasoning_effort string fields on any required sidecar, checked after identity validation and before the existing conflict check. Deliberately narrowed to these two fields (not also model_profile/policy_version, which are administrative metadata rather than execution provenance) so legitimate historical sidecars that never carried the latter two are not rejected; the real UTV2-1585 and UTV2-1586 fixtures and all existing sidecar fixtures in this test suite already carry both required fields and are unaffected.

RESOLVED (was ACCEPTED, not fixed -- PM correction: this is release-blocking, not a deferred follow-up): a third fresh-context independent review of the provenance-field fix confirmed no bypass, but noted the check only required model/reasoning_effort to be non-empty strings, not that they match the lane manifest's own model_routing.model/model_routing.reasoning_effort fields -- so a sidecar with well-formed but fabricated/copy-pasted values from a different lane would still pass. Initially deferred as a follow-up; PM directed that this be fixed in this PR. rebindModelRoutingJsonSha now requires exact agreement between the sidecar and manifest.model_routing for model/reasoning_effort whenever the manifest supplies a model_routing block, and additionally validates model_profile/policy_version whenever both sides carry a value for them, failing closed with a new sidecar_manifest_routing_mismatch code identifying the offending field before any proof write. When the manifest has no model_routing block at all, the cross-check is skipped -- ordinary closeout for lanes without one is unaffected.

RESOLVED (was ACCEPTED, not fixed): the same review noted the historical fixture tests in scripts/ops/proof-generate.test.ts synthesized an equivalent payload via preMergeModelRoutingJson() rather than reading the real committed model-routing.json files directly. This was fixed incidentally while implementing the sidecar/manifest routing cross-check (both fixture tests now fs.readFileSync the real committed sidecar). A later independent review found the manifest-side half of that same fix was still tautological: the fixture constructed its comparison manifest.model_routing by copying fields out of the sidecar it had just read, rather than reading the real docs/06_status/lanes/<issue>.json manifest file -- unable to catch a future drift between the two real, independently-authored files even though it looked like a real-data test. Fixed: both fixture tests now read the real lane manifest file directly and use its actual model_routing block.

RESOLVED (a fifth review finding, showing the second scope amendment was incomplete): an automated Codex review found the push-only restriction on 'Bind proof artifacts to merge SHA' did not cover every case -- a governed manifest-only repair PR (buildRepairRequiredViaPrPacket's recommended path for a lane whose pr_url is already set, e.g. UTV2-1586) merges via an ordinary push, and that push's own github.sha is the repair PR's merge commit, not the lane's original implementation merge SHA, even though github.event_name == 'push' is true. The manifest checked out by that same push already carries the correct historical commit_sha (the repair PR's whole point), so the step would still bind model-routing.json to the wrong SHA and hit the identical binding_conflict deadlock later in the same run. Fixed by additionally comparing the checked-out manifest's own commit_sha against this push's SHA and skipping the early bind when they already disagree -- the signal that this push is a repair commit, not the lane's own first-time closeout.

CLOSED: a sixth, final fresh-context independent review did a from-scratch adversarial pass over the full diff specifically hunting for a sixth variant of the same deadlock class (bot-actor self-retrigger, a stale-but-coincidentally-matching commit_sha, concurrent/overlapping workflow runs, interaction with the workflow's other two guard steps), ran the full 261-test suite plus type-check plus lint, and confirmed scope is clean (no changes to truth-check-lib.ts, merge-gate.yml, or docs/governance/). It found no blocking issue and no further deadlock variant -- every path it traced either resolves safely by design (repairMergedLaneManifest always re-resolves the authoritative PR/SHA from GitHub before any write, and nothing reaches main unless ops:lane-close exits 0) or reduces to an already-known, differently-classified failure (infra_error for a still-null pr_url). It flagged one wording-only nitpick in the workflow comment (the illustrative 'e.g. UTV2-1586' read as a claim about that lane's specific recovery path rather than the general precondition), fixed in a comment-only follow-up commit with no behavior change.
